title: Mystery Is My Hobby
paragraphs: A syndicated mystery series centered on crime writer and amateur detective Barton Drake, who becomes involved in murder investigations and helps unravel cases through observation and deduction.

Crime/mystery drama centered on mystery writer and amateur sleuth Barton Drake with police companion Inspector Noah Danton. Surviving material circulated through syndication packages that reused stories and program numbers, making universal episode numbering and many air dates unsafe.
GRH documents the program through Murder Is My Hobby network identity (1945 to 1946) and Mystery Is My Hobby syndicated packages (1947 to 1949).

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Glenn Langan (performer on 3 recordings), Norman Field (performer on 3 recordings), Betty Lou Gerson (performer on 1 recording), Bruce Buehl (announcer on 1 recording), Dave Titus (director on 1 recording), Fred Howard (writer on 1 recording), and Jack Edwards Jr. (performer on 1 recording).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include murder and homicide, deception, false identity and framing, wealth, valuables and inheritance, marriage, spouses and family conflict, artists, writing and media, and politics, elections and public office.
GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Postwar radio detective and mystery boom, Repackaged syndicated radio drama, and Mystery-writer detective protagonist.
